title: Methodological Obstacles, API Deprecations, and Empirical Null-Results in Weak-Drive Coherence Anchoring on Superconducting Processors
description:
Empirical evaluation and methodological null-result of the Quantum Anchor protocol on IBM Quantum (156-qubit Heron ibm_marrakesh) and IQM Resonance (20-qubit Garnet) superconducting processors. Evaluates API deprecations (removal of OpenPulse and analog IQ access), circuit-tautology traps, and empirical coherence noise floors across multi-qubit registers.

Tesseract-V3 five-phase sweep (IQM Garnet, 2026-10-08, one 1024-shot job per phase; counts 13, 3, 2, 14, 3; total 35/5120 = 0.684%). Chi-square on counts (not percentages): vs flat 20.29 (df = 4, p = 4.4e-4), so the five phases differ; vs fitted cos(8φ) 8.53 (df = 3 for two fitted parameters, p = 0.036); vs the parameter-free ideal prediction (1 + cos 8φ)/128, 11.44 (df = 5, Monte Carlo p = 0.047). Phases 2 and 3 have identical predictions but gave 2 vs 14 counts (exact p = 0.0042). With one job per phase, phase is confounded with job and calibration, so the cause of the differences is not identified. Evidence grade: C, cos(8φ) modulation not established on hardware.

Erratum 2026-11-18: earlier versions computed both chi-square values on percentages (1.9810 and 0.8331) and printed the ideal prediction a factor of two too high (maximum 3.125% instead of 1.5625%). The "Phase 0 repeat" entries re-download the same job and are not an independent repeat. Thanks to K. Indahl (Heuremen LLC) for the independent recount.
